builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Physics-Informed Sinusoidal Representation Networks for Damage Identification in Ultrasonic Guided Wave Structural Health Monitoring
summary: Replaces purely data-driven MLP surrogates for ultrasonic guided-wave damage identification with a frequency-domain physics-informed SIREN trained on sparse measurements without temporal discretization. Costs include implementing Mindlin-Reissner plate PDE residuals and a three-phase Adam/RAR/L-BFGS training schedule, which adds engineering complexity beyond a standard regression model. Can fail when the assumed plate theory does not match the structure, when measurement sparsity exceeds what the physics prior can compensate, and the single-notched-plate validation gives limited evidence of generalization.
rationale: This is a scientific-ML surrogate for structural health monitoring, not a technique applicable to the reader's LLM/ML production workload under constrained infrastructure.
technique: Physics-informed SIREN for ultrasonic wavefield reconstruction

claims.statement: Replaces purely data-driven MLP surrogates for ultrasonic guided-wave damage identification with a frequency-domain physics-informed SIREN trained on sparse measurements without temporal discretization. Costs include implementing Mindlin-Reissner plate PDE residuals and a three-phase Adam/RAR/L-BFGS training schedule, which adds engineering complexity beyond a standard regression model. Can fail when the assumed plate theory does not match the structure, when measurement sparsity exceeds what the physics prior can compensate, and the single-notched-plate validation gives limited evidence of generalization.
Localizes a milled notch from sparse experimental measurements with a localization error of 1% of the plate diagonal; tanh-MLP baselines, with and without Fourier features, fail to identify damage.
